newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan shilling gains vs dlr on agriculture flows.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan shilling gains vs dlr on agriculture flows.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling strengthened further against the dollar on Wednesday as large inflows from the agricultural sector flooded the market amid continued low importer demand, commercial dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 56.305 against the dollar from 56.40 on Tuesday. On the pound, it was posted at an average of 87.62 from 87.80 on Tuesday.
"The shilling reached (the) 56.10/30 level after an influx of large sell orders by exporters particulary from the tea and coffee traders," a commercial banker said.
"Importers, on the other hand, had no firm orders. And the few that had, chose to delay purchasing until next week," she said.

"Central Bank of Kenya intervention eased the rally on the shilling only temporarily to the levels of 56.25/45. As the market supply is seen to outstrip demand the near-term view of the local unit should continue to be bullish," she added.
Dealers said overnight money markets rates edged lower to the 15-18 percent levels.
